0.en: The dispute of the church with the state

en: a) The civil laws concern the security of the person and of the property of every citizen, whereby his religious opinions by no means come into consideration; to whatever faith he is therefore attached, it is the duty of the state to protect his rights as a citizen, and he can lose these in relation to the state only if he violates the rights of others; in that case the state asserts against him, and treats him according to, the maxims that the citizen gives expression to; with regard to faith he can bind himself to nothing toward the state, for the state is not capable of making or accepting such conditions.
zh: a) 市民法律关系到每个市民的人身和财产的安全，他的宗教见解在这里根本不予考虑；所以不管他信奉什么信仰，国家都有义务保护他作为市民的权利，而只有在他侵犯了别人的权利时，他才会对国家失去这些权利；这时国家就拿出市民自己所表露的那些准则来对付他，并照此对待他；至于信仰，他对国家不能承担任何约束，因为国家没有能力提出或接受这样的条件。

en: But on the other side all members of this state are united in one church; and as a society it has the right to exclude from itself anyone who will not put up with its laws.

Now the citizen who does not have the faith of the church, or leaves it, demands from the state as a right [his] capacity to exercise civil rights; but the church excludes him from its community and, because it embraces the whole state, at the same time from the state.

Which party, then, asserts its right — the civil state, which has taken upon itself the duty of securing the good citizen in his rights (and with regard to its laws we will and can take him for good, whatever faith he may have) and cannot enter into faith at all, or the church state, which has the right to exclude a person of another faith from its community, and thus also excludes him from the state?

In almost all Catholic as well as Protestant lands the church state has asserted its rights against the civil state; and no person of another faith is capable in them of attaining civil rights, nor of enjoying the protection of the laws in criminal as well as civil cases, which a citizen enjoys; he can acquire no kind of landed property, can administer no office of the state, and is treated differently also with regard to taxes; even since baptism is not merely an ecclesiastical actus by which one enters the church, but is also a civil actus, whereby the existence of the child is made known to the state and at least as many rights are claimed from it as the church will permit, the church compels the father of the child, whose faith differs from the faith of the church of the land, to have it baptised according to its customs and by one of its officials — which the church does not do in the sense that it thereby takes the child into its bosom, for it afterwards leaves it entirely to the father to have it brought up in his religion, but it only proves thereby that it has taken from the civil state the right to receive citizens; in that its baptism, in the case of the child of a follower of the ruling church, is reception both into its bosom and into the state. — The similar case also occurs with marriage, which in many lands, in order to be valid, is likewise performed only by an official of the ruling church; whereby the latter does not obtrude itself to perform a ceremony of the foreign faith to which those being married adhere, but performs a civil act.
Thus the civil state has ceded its rights and its office to the church state, both when the two come into collision and when there is a two-sided action, where the sanction of both is required.
zh: 但另一方面，这个国家的所有成员又都联合在一个教会里；教会作为一个团体，有权把任何不愿接受它的法规的人从自己这里排除出去。
于是，那个没有教会信仰、或者脱离了教会的市民，向国家要求承认他有行使市民权利的能力，并把这当作一项权利；但教会却把他从自己的团体中排除出去，又因为它囊括了整个国家，所以就同时把他从国家中排除出去。
那么，是哪一方在主张自己的权利呢？——是市民国家，它承担了义务，要保障好市民的权利（就它的法律而言，不管他信奉什么信仰，我们都愿意、也能够把他看作好市民），而它根本不能去过问信仰的事；还是教会国家，它有权把一个信仰不同的人从自己的团体中排除出去，因而也把他从国家中排除出去？

在几乎所有的天主教国家和新教国家里，教会国家都对市民国家主张了自己的权利；在那里，任何信仰不同的人都不能获得市民权利，也不能像市民那样在刑事案件和民事案件中受到法律的保护；他不能购置任何种类的地产，不能担任国家的任何职务，在纳税上也受到不同的对待；甚至，洗礼不只是使人进入教会的教会行为，而且也是一种市民行为，通过它把孩子的存在告知国家，并至少向国家要求教会所允许的那些权利，所以教会就强迫那个信仰与本国教会信仰不同的孩子的父亲，按教会的习俗、由教会的职员给孩子施洗；教会这样做并不是要把孩子收进自己的怀抱，因为事后它完全把孩子交给父亲，让他按自己的宗教去教育，而只是借此证明，它已经把接纳市民的权利从市民国家手里夺走了；因为对于占统治地位教会的信徒的孩子来说，它的洗礼就是既收进自己的怀抱，也收进国家。——类似的情形也发生在婚姻上：在许多国家里，婚姻要有效，也只能由占统治地位的教会的职员来主持；这时教会并不硬要去履行结婚者所信奉的那种外来信仰的仪式，而是做一件市民的事情。
所以，市民国家已经把自己的权利和职权让给了教会国家，不论是在两者发生冲突的时候，还是在需要双方批准的那种双方行为上，都是如此。

en: In a similar way as the church behaves toward the state, the guilds and their rights also behave toward it.
These too form a society within the state, to which their members cede certain rights and, by entering into it, take on certain duties.
Such a guild in a city thus embraces all who are of the same trade, and by the right of a society has the right to admit whom it will and to exclude whoever does not submit to its regulations.

Now on the other side the state has the duty to protect everyone who, without offending the civil laws (and these for their part can determine nothing about guilds), wants to earn his living in whatever way; but if the guild does not permit it to him, thus excludes him from itself, then it at the same time excludes him from the whole community and robs him of a right that the state permits him, hinders him from exercising a civil right; and in this too the state has renounced the right of its citizens.
zh: 教会对国家采取什么态度，行会及其权利对国家也采取类似的态度。
行会也在国家里组成一个团体，成员向它让出某些权利，并通过加入它而承担某些义务。
一座城市里的这样一个行会，因此包括所有从事同一手艺的人，并且按团体的权利，有权接纳它愿意接纳的人，排除不愿服从它的规章的人。
而另一方面，国家有义务保护每一个想以不论什么方式谋生、又不触犯市民法律的人（而市民法律本身对行会作不出任何规定）；但若行会不允许他这样做，也就是把他从自己这里排除出去，那么行会就同时把他从整个共同体中排除出去，夺走了国家允许他享有的权利，妨碍他行使一项市民权利；在这件事上，国家也就此放弃了自己市民的权利。

en: In the same way the state has the right to take into its service as such an official whomever it wants to use for the scholarly education of its youth, whomever it finds fit for it; but the members of every branch of learning have united into a guild, and such a guild asserts the right to admit or to exclude, according as its laws are accepted or not; and because one who was not a guild member would be excluded by this society, and thus at the same time in that respect by the state, the state has given up its right and is compelled to take as its learned officials such as have become masters (magistri or doctores) in the guild of this branch of the sciences, or at least compels such an official afterwards to have himself admitted into their guild; and if he had no inclination for it, while the guild nevertheless wants to assert its right, then it makes him a present of this mastership, an honour which he then cannot well refuse, or would refuse only out of sheer bizarrerie.
zh: 同样，国家有权把它想用来对青年进行科学教育的人、它认为合用的人，聘为这样的公职；但各门学问的成员都联合成了一个行会，而行会主张自己有接纳或排除的权利，要看它的章程是否被接受；而既然一个不属于行会的人会被这个团体、因而也就同时在这个意义上被国家排除在外，那么国家就已经放弃了自己的权利，不得不聘用那些在这个学科行会里当上了师傅（magistri 或 doctores）的人来做自己的学问官员，或者至少迫使这样一位官员事后让自己被接进行会；如果他对此没有兴趣，而行会又偏要主张自己的权利，那么行会就拿这个师傅名号送他一个人情，这种荣誉他多半不好拒绝，除非他纯粹出于古怪脾气才会拒绝。

en: If therefore in recent times the concession of civil rights to non-Catholics by some Catholic governments, the appointment of their own clergy and the building of their own churches, has been praised on the one side as a magnanimous tolerance, while on the other side it has been asserted that the word tolerance, forbearance, used here is quite out of place, that what has happened is mere justice, then these contradictions can be reconciled as follows: on the part of the state, the concession of these rights was indisputably nothing more than the removal of a great injustice and therefore a duty; on the part of the church, however, which has the right to exclude those of another faith not, to be sure, from air, soil and water, as it once asserted and here and there still asserts, but yet from the state, it is always tolerance, and when the state demands it as a duty to respect the rights of those of another faith, the officials of the tolerant (also Protestant) church always speak of forbearance, of compassion, of love, which one must show toward those in error, of inclinations which cannot be commanded as duties, but which one ought to show them voluntarily.
zh: 所以，如果说近来某些天主教政府给予非天主教徒市民权利、允许他们有自己的教士、建自己的教堂，一方面被称赞为宽宏大量的宽容，另一方面又有人主张：这里用宽容、容忍这个词根本不合宜，所发生的事不过是公正罢了——那么这些矛盾可以这样统一起来：从国家方面说，给予这些权利无疑只不过是取消一桩极大的不公正，因而是一种义务；但从教会方面说，教会虽然无权像它从前、如今在这里那里还主张的那样，把信仰不同的人排除于空气、土地和水之外，却有权把他排除于国家之外，所以这始终是宽容；而当国家要求把尊重信仰不同者的权利当作义务时，宽容的（也包括新教的）教会的职员们总还是讲照顾、讲同情、讲对迷误者应当表现的爱，讲那些不能作为义务来要求、而只能自愿对他们表示的偏好。

en: b) For the celebration of their divine service, for their instruction in religious matters, all congregations need special buildings, special teachers and otherwise still some persons; for the erection of the former and the maintenance of both the whole people, and for the embellishment of some liturgical vessels individuals, have paid voluntary dues and contributions; the buildings erected, the fixed salaries and incomes of the teachers and other church servants are therefore a property of the congregations, of the people in general, [not] of the state; but they have almost always been regarded as a property of the state in so far as the latter, or in so far as many congregations generally, have united into a church state; this distinction, whether the churches and the incomes of church servants are a property of the state, as civil or as church state, is of no consequence and does not show itself either, as long as only one church is found in a state; but the difference at once strikes the eye and gives occasion for quarrel as soon as different churches settle there.
zh: b) 各教团要庆祝自己的礼拜、要在宗教事务上教导人，都需要专门的建筑、专门的教师，此外还需要一些人；为了建造前者、为了供养这两者，全体民众，为了装饰某些礼拜器具，则有一些个人，都缴纳了自愿的捐税和献款；所以，建起来的房屋、教师和其他教会仆役的固定薪俸和收入，是各教团、是全体民众的财产，〔不是〕国家的财产；但只要国家本身、或者说只要许多教团一般地联合成一个教会国家，这些财产就几乎总是被看作国家的财产；至于教会和教会仆役的收入究竟是国家——作为市民国家还是作为教会国家——的财产，这种区分无关紧要，在一个国家里只存在一个教会时也显不出来；但一旦有不同的教会迁入定居，这种区别就立刻显而易见，并且引起争执。

en: The church that is only now gaining ground demands, on grounds taken from civil rights, a share in this property of the state; and the state is obliged to grant to the congregations, whatever faith they adhere to, churches for their divine service and to appoint teachers according to their mind; whereas the church that has hitherto been ruling asserts its right to the property transferred to it and never disputed — if the state has strength enough to assert its right and if its administrators are insightful, impartial and just enough to know this right of theirs and to want to assert it, then it will grant every church the means, according to its needs, to hold its divine service according to its own mind.

Although now a state, as civil state, and its legislators and administrators as such ought to have no faith, it nevertheless usually happens that, as members of the ruling church, they are laid upon by it as a duty to protect the rights of the ruling church; and the dispute between the two churches is usually not decided according to the rights of the state, but usually by violence on the one side and necessity on the other.

For if the church that is nesting itself in spreads so much that, in asserting the rights of the church in dispute — rights that could be maintained only by exterminating the adherents of the new doctrine, or at least only by great acts of violence and great expense — too great a harm would arise for the state and too deep an offence against its laws and rights, then it is thereby reminded of its danger and concedes some rights to the new church, but in doing so uses the language of the church and calls this tolerance; — or the dispute is settled in another way, namely that the church hitherto suppressed becomes ruling and then the hitherto ruling one becomes merely the tolerated one, then the state commonly enters again into the same covenant with the now ruling church and asserts its rights again as unrestrictedly as it did those of the previous one.

It is evident from this, as from what was said above, that the remark which many acute historians have made, that, to one's astonishment, every church, unmindful of the sufferings it has endured — the remembrance of which should have made it tolerant — became intolerant as soon as it became ruling, — that this remark is not merely a contingent proposition abstracted from history and experience, but that it follows of itself with compelling necessity from the rights of every church — which consists in the right of every society to exclude from its society those who do not submit to the laws and ordinances of the society; if therefore it becomes ruling in a state, then this church society asserts its right and excludes the person of another faith from its community and thereby at the same time from the state, and becomes intolerant both with regard to faith and with regard to the property of the non-ruling church.
zh: 那个刚刚站稳脚跟的教会，根据从市民权利中取来的理由，要求分享国家的这份财产；而国家有义务向各教团——不论它们信奉什么信仰——提供做礼拜的教堂，并按它们的意愿安排教师；反之，一直占统治地位的教会则主张自己对那份转让给它、从未引起争议的财产拥有权利；如果国家有足够的力量主张自己的权利，它的管理者也足够明察、公正、正直，能认识并愿意主张自己的这项权利，那么国家就会按各教会的需要，给它们提供按自己的意愿做礼拜的手段。
一个国家作为市民国家，它的立法者和管理者作为这样的人，本来不该有什么信仰，但事情通常还是这样：他们作为占统治地位教会的成员，被这个教会当作义务加在身上，要去保护占统治地位教会的权利；于是两个教会之间的争执通常不是按国家的法来裁断，而通常是一方动武、另一方受逼迫。

因为，如果那个正在悄悄落户的教会扩展得太厉害，以致在维护争执中教会的权利时——这些权利只有靠消灭新教义的追随者，或者至少只有靠大规模的暴力和大笔花费才能维持——会给国家造成太大的损害，太深地冒犯它的法律和权利，那么国家就因此被提醒到自己的危险，让给新教会一些权利，但同时又用教会的腔调说话，把这叫作宽容；——或者争执以另一种方式了结：迄今受压迫的教会成了占统治地位的，于是迄今占统治地位的只成了被容忍的；这时国家通常又同现在占统治地位的教会结成同样的同盟，又像从前对待前一个教会那样毫无限制地主张它的权利。

从这里，正如从上面所说的话里，可以看出：许多敏锐的历史学家所作的评论——说令人诧异的是，每个教会一旦占了统治地位，就忘记了自己所受过的苦难（记住这些苦难本该使它宽容），因而也变得不宽容了——这个评论并不只是从历史和经验中抽象出来的一句偶然的话，而是以不可抗拒的必然性从每个教会自身的权利中得出来的——这权利就在于，每个团体都有权把那些不服从团体的法律和规章的人从自己的团体中排除出去；所以，一旦教会在一个国家里占了统治地位，这个教会团体就主张自己的权利，把信仰不同的人从自己的团体中排除出去，因而也同时从国家中排除出去，并且在信仰方面、在不属于统治地位教会的财产方面，都变得不宽容。

en: This course of things with regard to the property of a church showed itself at the first spread of the Christian church and at the spread of every new sect within this church itself.

The Christians at first gathered in private houses, built their own places of worship at their own expense; but when they became ruling, the church made its rights valid, destroyed the pagan temples and took possession of them for itself, even if in a city or in a congregation the greater part were still pagans; a wholly Christian congregation had the right to do so according to the rights of the state; Julian asserted the church right and state right of the pagans and took back from the Christians the temples that they had taken from the pagans.

The Protestants used the hitherto Catholic churches for their divine service and applied the incomes of the clergy and monasteries according to their own mind; and [they] had the right to do so according to civil right and also made their church right valid — but thereby violated the Catholic church right, which this church still asserts, which regards the Protestant churches, bishoprics, monasteries and ecclesiastical incomes as something that is de jure its property, and consistently has its bishops, abbots — in partibus.

Two church rights cannot be legally settled against each other, since they stand in direct and irreconcilable contradiction; they can be settled only by violence or by the right of the state, which must then be conceded as a higher right — something the Catholic church concedes in no case, the Protestant only in some respects.
Whatever the one church concedes, it gives away something of its right, and on its side it is grace.
zh: 在教会财产方面事情的这种进程，在基督教最初传播的时候，在这教会内部每一个新教派传播的时候，都显现出来了。
基督徒起初在私人住宅里聚会，自费建造自己的礼拜场所；但当他们占了统治地位，教会就行使自己的权利，拆毁异教的庙宇，把它们据为己有，哪怕在一座城市里或一个教团里大多数人还是异教徒；一个完全由基督徒组成的教团，按国家的法是有权这样做的；尤利安则主张异教徒的教会权利和国家权利，又把基督徒从异教徒手里夺去的庙宇夺了回来。
新教徒把此前天主教的教堂拿来做自己的礼拜，并按自己的意愿使用教士和修道院的收入；按市民的法，他们有权这样做，也主张了自己的教会权利——但因此侵犯了天主教的教会权利，而天主教至今仍主张这种权利：它把新教的教堂、主教区、修道院和教会收入看作依法属于它的财产，并且一贯地保有它的主教和修道院长——名义上的（in partibus）。
两种教会权利彼此之间无法依法调解，因为它们处于直接而不可调和的对立之中；只能靠暴力或靠国家的法来调解，而国家的法这时必须被承认为一种更高的权利——天主教会在任何情况下都不承认这一点，新教会只在某些方面承认。
一个教会让出什么，就是放弃自己权利中的一点东西，从它这方面说，这就是恩典。

en: Whoever leaves the church of his land banishes himself from his fatherland with the loss of his civil liberties; and this way of proceeding might seem harsh and unjust — to persecute someone on account of his faith and to withdraw from him the enjoyment of his civil rights, to banish him from everything that nature and habit make dear to him.

But that no wrong is done to him by this, the church proves with the language of magnanimity, not merely of justice: that it did not stand in his way when he changed his faith; that it honours his freedom to want to leave it; but since a condition of the capacity to enjoy civil rights in this land is connection with the church, and this condition is now cancelled by the change of his faith, which he himself knew, no injustice at all is done to him in the matter; he had a free choice in this alternative.

If by this exclusion he were only excluded from the church, then it would thereby exclude only one who has already left it; but it thereby excludes him from the state as well; and the state admits that its rights are violated — the state and the church have in this respect melted into one.
zh: 谁离开本国的教会，就是丧失自己的市民自由、把自己逐出祖国；这种作法也许显得严厉而不公正：因为一个人的信仰就迫害他，剥夺他享有市民权利，把他从一切由天性和习惯而令他珍贵的东西那里放逐出去。
但教会用宽宏大量、而不只是公正的腔调证明，这样做并没有对他不公：他改变信仰时教会没有阻拦他；教会尊重他要退出的自由；可是，在这块土地上享有市民权利的一个条件，就是与教会保持联结，而这个条件现在因他改变信仰而被取消了，这一点他自己也知道，所以这里面根本没有对他不公；在这个二选一面前，他是自由选择的。
如果这种排除只是把他排除出教会，那么教会排除的就只是一个已经离开了它的人；但教会借此同时把他排除出国家；而国家竟容许自己的权利受到侵犯——在这个意义上，国家和教会已经熔为一体。

en: c) Every human being brings into the world, besides the right of animal preservation, also the right to develop his capacities, to become a human being; through this right parents and the state take over and share the duty of educating purposively; and the latter, besides this duty, would also have the greatest interest in so forming the young hearts of his growing state citizens that honour and advantage for him might one day grow out of their manly age.

Now a state has believed that it could satisfy this duty of its own and this interest of its own no better and more naturally than by entrusting this care either wholly or for the most part to the church, and in this way sufficient care is taken not only for the interest of the state but also for the interest of the church — namely that the young citizens be educated into citizens of the church as well; whether, however, the young citizens are thereby not endangered in their right to the free development of their powers depends solely on how the church performs its office in the matter. — As the state, which has already made the rights of the children, at least as persons, its own and has protected them as such, has the right over them to form them according to its maxims and its end, so the church asserts precisely this right, because it already lets the children enjoy its benefits, and thus makes them fit and, through instruction, inclined to perform their duties in time also toward the church.

If now, in the ripe age of understanding, a citizen does not find the laws or other condition of his fatherland suitable to him, then in most European states he has the free choice to leave it; and his dependence on the laws of his country is grounded on this free resolution of arbitrariness to live under them; however great a share habit or fear may have had in this resolution, they can yet never abolish the possibility of free choice.
zh: c) 每个人除了动物式保存自己的权利之外，还把自己培养自己的能力、成为一个人的权利带到世界上来；凭借这项权利，父母和国家把合乎目的地进行教育的义务接过来，并分担它；而国家除了这项义务之外，还有最大的利益，把正在成长的自己国家公民的年轻心灵塑造成这样：有朝一日能从他们的成年里为他长出荣誉和好处来。

一个国家于是相信，对自己这份义务和这份利益，它没有更好、更自然的办法来尽到，除非把这份操心整个地或大部分地交给教会；这样一来，不只是国家的利益、而且教会的利益——也把年轻公民教育成教会的公民——都得到了充分的照顾；但年轻公民会不会因此在他们自由培养各种力量的权利上受到危害，这完全取决于教会在其中怎样履行自己的职务。——国家已经把孩子们的权利、至少作为人的权利变成自己的权利，并且已经作为这样的权利加以保护，因此它对他们有按自己的准则、照自己的目的来塑造他们的权利；同样，教会也主张这项权利，因为它已经让孩子们享受它的善行，于是把他们弄得能干，又通过教导使他们有意愿，将来也对教会尽自己的义务。
如果一个公民在知性成熟的年纪，觉得自己祖国的法律或其他状况不合自己的意，那么在大多数欧洲国家里，他都有离开它的自由选择；而他对本国法律的依赖，就建立在这种愿意在它们之下生活的任意的自由决断上；习惯或恐惧在这决断上不管占了多少份，它们都永远不能取消自由选择的可能性。

en: If, however, the church had by its education brought it so far that it either wholly suppressed understanding and reason on the side of religious reflection or at least had filled the imagination with terrors in such a way that reason and understanding cannot and may not dare to become conscious of its freedom and to use it also on religious objects, then the church would have wholly taken away the possibility of the free choice and resolution to be its member, on which alone, after all, it can and will ground its claims upon anyone, would have violated the natural right of children to a free development of their capacities, and would have educated slaves for itself instead of free citizens.

Besides, now — however much power early impressions have over the imagination and hearts of children, and the power of the example of the most beloved persons and of those bound to us by the first bonds of nature, which takes place in every education without the freedom of reason having to be fettered by it — besides this, now, the church educates for faith, that is, understanding and reason are not so developed that they themselves would be guided to form their own principles or to judge according to their laws about what is presented to them, but the representations and words that are impressed on the imagination and memory are so armed with terrors and, in so holy, inviolable a dazzling light, brought forward with the command that partly before their brilliance the laws of understanding and reason must fall silent and may not be used, partly that they prescribe to understanding and reason laws that are therefore heterogeneous.

Through this alien legislation, then, freedom is taken from reason and understanding, that is, the capacity to follow laws that are proper to them and grounded in their nature; freedom of choice to enter the church no longer takes place; the state, however well it meant it, has become a traitor to the rights of children to a free development of the powers of the soul.

The expedient of educating children without the positive faith of a church, in order to preserve for them the freedom of choice for their riper age, would — without thinking of the countless difficulties of the possibility of carrying it out — also for binding reasons not be allowed to be adopted, because the church declares it partly a crime out of duty to leave children in such an ignorance in faith, partly it would be most laborious for it to make up what has been neglected in youth, and it is almost no longer possible to press faith so into the marrow of the soul, to wrap all branches of human concepts and capacities, all branches of human striving and willing, with it.

Hence the Patriarch (in Nathan [IV, 2]), when he hears that the Jew has brought the girl up not so much in his faith as in no faith at all, and has taught her about God no more and no less than reason suffices for, becomes most indignant at this and declares him for this reason worthy “to be burned three times over! — What? to let a child grow up without any faith? — How? not to teach a child the great duty of believing at all?
That is too much!”
zh: 但如果教会通过它的教育已经做到这一步：它在宗教思考这一方面要么把知性和理性完全压制下去，要么至少把想象力塞满了恐惧，以至理性和知性不敢也不许意识到自己的自由、不敢也不许把自由也用到宗教对象上去，那么教会就完全拿走了自由选择和决断做它成员的可能性——而它对任何人的要求，本来只可能也只想建立在这一点上——，就侵犯了孩子们自由培养自己能力的自然权利，给自己教育出来的就是奴隶，而不是自由公民。

此外——早期印象对孩子们的想象力和心灵有多大力量，最受疼爱、通过自然的最初纽带同我们连在一起的人的榜样有多大力量，这在每一种教育里都会发生，而不必因此就把理性的自由锁住——，除此之外，教会是在培养信仰，也就是说，知性和理性并不是这样被发展起来，使它们自己受到引导去形成独特的原则、或按照自己的法律去判断摆到它们面前的东西，而是那些印进想象力和记忆里的表象和词语，被这样用恐惧武装起来，在一种如此神圣、不可侵犯、令人目眩的光亮中连同命令一起被带出来，以致一部分是：在它们的光辉面前，知性和理性的法律必须沉默，不许被使用；一部分是：它们给知性和理性规定了因此是异质的法律。
通过这种外来的立法，理性和知性就被夺走了自由，也就是被夺走了遵循那些为它们所固有、建立在它们本性之中的法律的能力；进入教会的选择自由不再存在；国家不管用意多么好，都成了孩子们自由培养灵魂各种能力这一权利的叛卖者。

让孩子不接受某个教会的实证信仰长大，以便为他们更成熟的年纪保住选择自由，这个办法——且不去想实行起来有无数的困难——即使从有约束力的理由来看也不能被采纳，因为教会一方面宣布，让孩子留在这样一种信仰上的无知里，是一种出于义务的罪行；另一方面，要把少年时耽误的东西补回来，对教会来说极其费力，而且几乎再也不可能把信仰这样压进灵魂的骨髓，用它把人类概念和能力的一切枝杈、人类追求和意愿的一切枝杈都缠裹起来。
所以《智者纳坦》里的宗主教（第 IV 幕第 2 场），一听说这个犹太人把这女孩不是养在他的信仰里、倒不如说是养在没有任何信仰里，关于上帝教给她的不多不少、只到理性够用为止，就为此最恼火，并因此宣布他活该“被烧死三次！——什么？让一个孩子没有半点信仰地长大？——怎么？信仰这条大义务，竟完全不教给孩子？
这太过分了！”

en: For there is a much greater hope of bringing a human being whose understanding has from youth on been accustomed to the duty of believing to the faith of another church, than of bringing a human being whose imagination is free from its images and whose understanding is free from its fetters to faith at all and to obedience under the opinions that a church demands.
zh: 因为，要把一个知性从少年时起就习惯了对信仰的义务的人，带到另一个教会的信仰里去，比起把一个人根本带向信仰、带向服从一个教会所要求的那些意见之下去——而这个人的想象力摆脱了它的图像，他的知性摆脱了它的锁链——，希望要大得多。

en: Two remarks can still be added: that, although whoever wants to become a citizen of a Christian state must adopt the faith of the land, yet conversely a proselyte is not for that reason a citizen of the state, for the natural reason that the church has a greater extent than the state and the latter nevertheless everywhere still asserts independent rights.
(In what case were the proselyti portae of the Hebrews?)
zh: 还可以补充两点说明：虽然谁想成为一个基督教国家的公民，就必须接受这个国家的信仰，但反过来，一个皈依者并不因此就是这个国家的公民，自然的理由在于，教会的范围比国家更大，而国家毕竟到处都还主张自己有独立的权利。
（希伯来人的 proselyti portae 是在哪种情形下？）

en: Further: the object of the contract that lies at the basis of a church is faith and opinion.

In the Protestant church, especially in more recent times, freedom in this respect is so much greater than in the Catholic that it admits of no comparison; but in both the rights flowing from this contract are strictly asserted.

In the Catholic church opinion is guarded with just the same exactness; in the Protestant church, by contrast, it is well known that the faith of the most learned and most upright theologians is by no means the same as what they sign or swear to in the symbolic books; of other officials of the civil state it is in any case almost always the case that they know the doctrines of the symbolic books, which they likewise must sign, very little; whoever, for example, did not hold the same opinion of baptism as is set up by the church, or thought quite differently from the church about the main points of Protestant dogmatics, is not asked further about it, even if he has already brought this to light in writings or otherwise publicly; if he, however, wanted to be so consistent and not have his child baptized or, on taking up an office, not sign the symbolic books, then the church, which has lodged no protest against his opinion, would nevertheless seize the consequences that naturally flow from it and assert its rights.
zh: 其次：作为教会基础的那份契约，它的对象是信仰和意见。
在新教教会里，尤其在较近的时代，这方面的自由比天主教教会里大得多，根本不能相比；但在两者那里，从这份契约流出的权利都被严格主张。

在天主教教会里，意见受到同样精确的看管；在新教教会里则众所周知，最博学、最正直的神学家的信仰，根本不是他们在信条书里签字或宣誓承认的那个信仰；至于市民国家的其他官员，情形反正几乎总是这样：他们对自己同样必须签字的信条书的学说知道得极少；比如，谁要是对洗礼不持教会所提出的那种意见，或者对新教教义学的主要各点想得跟教会完全不同，人们就不再追问他这件事，即使他已经在著作里或别处公开表露过；但他要是这样彻底，不肯给自己的孩子施洗，或者在接任一个职务时不肯在信条书上签字，那么，教会虽然对他的意见没有提出过抗议，却会把他意见中自然流出的后果据为己有，并主张自己的权利。

15.en: The Contract of the Church. Representation, Active Citizens on Doctrine
15.zh: 教会的契约。代表（制），积极公民论教义

en: As for the contract itself, on which the rights of the church itself rest, the first rights of princes could indeed rest on the rights of the conqueror who left the conquered their life on the condition of obedience, and on this original contract of the victor with the vanquished the rights of the descendants of those princes could be founded, which they would then possess no longer through the right of conquerors but through the right of inheritance, just as on that contract also rested the subjection of the will of the individual to the will of the sovereign — a theory whose assertion or refutation is indifferent to us here — yet this much remains, that it lies in the nature of civil society, however it and the rights of its rulers and legislators may have arisen, that in it the rights of the individual have become rights of the state, that the state binds itself to assert and protect my rights as its own.

With the rights of the church as a state, by contrast, there can be no doubt that, at least in the formation of the same, its contract and its rights were grounded solely on the voluntary consent of all individuals.

In this state the general will, that is, the majority of votes, is expressed as laws of faith; and the society unites for the protection of this faith, one for all and all for one; partly for the organization and order of the general assembly in which the laws are made, partly for the protection of these laws of faith, to which above all instruction of every kind and public worship belong, the church state needs officials and has set them up.
zh: 至于教会自身的权利所依据的那份契约本身，诸侯最初的权利固然可以建立在征服者的权利上——征服者让被征服者以服从为条件保住性命——，而诸侯后裔的权利就可以建立在这份战胜者与被战胜者的原初契约上，他们于是不再凭征服者的权利、而是凭继承权占有这些权利，正如个人的意志服从主权者的意志也建立在那份契约上一样——这个理论是主张还是反驳，我们在这里无所谓——，但有一点仍然成立：不管市民社会及其统治者和立法者的权利是怎样产生的，市民社会的本性就在于，在它里面个人的权利已经变成了国家的权利，国家有义务把我的权利当作它自己的权利来主张和保护。
相反，就教会作为一个国家的权利而言，无可怀疑的是：至少在教会形成的时候，它的契约和它的权利只建立在所有个人的自愿同意上。
在这个国家里，普遍意志，也就是多数票，被表述为信仰的法律；而社会结合在一起来保护这个信仰，一人为一切、一切为一人；一部分是为了组织和维持制定法律的大会的秩序，一部分是为了保护这些信仰法律——其中首先包括各种教导和公开的礼拜——，教会国家需要官员，并且把官员设立了起来。

en: With regard to the one point, the agreement of all in one faith, it now makes a very great difference whether the contract of the church is regarded in such a way that its union has arisen of itself out of the agreement of the faith of all, and whether in the general faith only the faith of all is expressed, or whether this has also been partly fixed by the majority of votes and whether this has been accepted as possible.

The latter principle has been solemnly adopted by the Catholic church, in that the highest power is entrusted to church assemblies to decide in the last instance what the faith of the church is, and it is indeed the majority of votes that a respective minority has the indispensable duty to submit to.
In such an assembly the members are present partly as representatives of their flock, partly, and above all, as officials of the church.

Their authority is indeed supposed to flow from their character as representatives, but the people has long since lost the right, which it had for several centuries, of itself choosing its representatives and officials.

The officials of the church, who in turn are appointed by officials or in part by a corps equally independent of the people, thus constitute the assembly of the church, and all together form an organization complete in itself, which handles, determines and rules the faith of the people, of the laity, without the latter being granted the slightest influence in the matter any longer. — Since the object of the church is not person and property, which are capable of having force used to protect them, but opinion and faith, it is entirely contrary to the nature of opinion that the individual should subject to the majority of votes what his own is, and what is possible in the civil contract, to subject one's will to the general will and to regard this as law for oneself, can absolutely not produce any such church contract, that is, a contract about faith — such a one is in itself impossible and, if it has nevertheless been made, entirely null and void.
zh: 就所有人在一个信仰上取得一致这一点而言，教会的契约究竟是被看作这样——它的结合自动地从所有人信仰的一致中产生出来，在普遍的信仰里表达的只是所有人的信仰——，还是说这个信仰也有一部分是由多数票确定下来的、并且这一点被当作可能的而接受，这中间的差别非常之大。
后一条原则被天主教教会郑重地采纳了，因为最高的权力被交托给教会会议，由它在最后一审中决定什么是教会的信仰，而且少数派无论何时都负有不可推卸的义务去服从的，正是多数票。
在这样一个会议里，成员们一部分是作为自己牧群的代表在场，一部分则首先是作为教会的官员在场。
他们的全权固然应当从他们作为代表的身份中流出，但人民早就失去了它曾拥有过几百年的权利：自己选举自己的代表和官员。

教会的官员又由官员、或部分地由一个同样不依赖人民的团体任命，他们于是构成教会的会议，而所有人合起来形成一个自身完整的组织，它操持、规定并统治人民、即俗人的信仰，不再允许后者在其中有一点点影响。——由于教会的对象不是人身和财产——这些东西可以成为使用暴力来保护的对象——，而是意见和信仰，所以，个人把自己所持的东西交给多数票去决定，这完全违背意见的本性；而在市民契约里可能的事——把自己的意志交给普遍意志、并把这个普遍意志看作对自己有效的法律——，绝对产生不出这样一种教会契约，即一种关于信仰的契约——这样一种契约本身就是不可能的，即使它还是被订立了，也完全是无效的、作废的。

en: If the assembly consists of representatives who are such not merely in name but also in deed, that is, who have really been chosen as such by the congregations, then no other authority can be given them than a declaration of what the faith of the congregation is and which articles it regards as the main points, as the conditions under whose equality alone it is willing to regard itself as joined with other congregations as one church; to give them the authority to determine the faith of the congregation according to their insight and to subject this to the majority of votes would form a representative republic that would entirely contradict the right of human beings not to subject their opinions to an alien authority and would put them in the same case in which they would be under the contract just considered — which constitution one could call a pure democracy. — Such a representative republic, then, was the church in the first centuries of its spread, and one beholds in this a strange conflict of the principle of the freedom of the opinions of each individual congregation and its representative with the principle that it is a duty to subject oneself to the majority of votes.

For if there were divisions, which, as is well known, were lacking in no period, both parties appealed to a free general council and demanded this while accepting the principle that it is a duty to submit to the majority, whereby each part had the hope of winning the others over to itself through its cogent reasons and eloquence and still more through its intrigues, also the assistance of power; the victorious part then demanded the application of this principle and the submission of the minority, while the latter now usually took refuge in the other principle and cried out about the violence that was to be done to the freedom of its conviction.

Very often there were also special associations for carrying through their purpose, whose members now made up a moral person, and the conclusions of the assembly can then no longer be regarded as the conclusions of a free majority but as the victory of a faction that permitted itself deceit and every kind of violence in order to carry its cause through and frightfully maltreated the defeated party as rebels; an assembly of holy fathers of this kind was called a robber band by its opponents, and Mosheim, [Institutiones] Hist[oriae] eccl[esiasticae] saec.
5, pars 2, c. 5, § 14, has only this to object to this harsh expression, that it has not also been used of some other church assemblies that deserved this title just as well.

But since the laity have also lost the right even to be represented with regard to their faith, since the bishops and heads of the Christian church are mere officials, since then the laws of faith have been made entirely by their rulers, and it can be rather indifferent — not indeed to the bishops, but to the people — whether its ruler and judge in faith is one person — the pope — or a multitude of persons independent of it, whether its spiritual constitution is a monarchy or an aristocracy: its rights are in both cases equally great, equally nil.
To lose a word about the lawfulness of such a government, of such a constitution in matters of faith, would be completely useless.
zh: 如果会议是由这样的代表组成——他们不只是名义上的、而且事实上也是代表，也就是说，他们在现实中是被各教团选为这样的代表的——，那么能随同交给他们的全权，就无非是一份声明：教团的信仰是什么，它把哪些条款看作主要各点、看作这样的条件：只有在这些条件的平等之下，它才愿意与其他教团一起把自己看作一个教会；要是交给他们全权，让他们按自己的见识去规定教团的信仰、并把这个信仰交给多数票去决定，那就会形成一个代议制共和国，它与人不把自己的意见交给外来权威的权利完全矛盾，并使他们陷入他们在那份刚刚考察过的契约下所处的同样境地——这种宪制，人们可以叫作纯粹的民主制。——教会在它传播的最初几个世纪里，就是这样一个代议制共和国，而人们在这里看到，每个单个教团及其代表在意见自由上的原则，与服从多数票是一种义务这一原则，发生了一种奇特的冲突。
因为一旦出现分裂——众所周知，没有一个时期缺过分裂——，双方就都向一个自由的大公会议发出呼吁，并在接受服从多数是一种义务这一原则的同时提出这个要求，这时每一方都抱着希望，想靠自己有分量的理由和口才、更靠自己的阴谋，还有权力的帮助，把对方争取到自己这边来；得胜的一方这时就要求运用这条原则、要求少数派服从，而少数派这时通常就求助于另一条原则，大声叫喊说有人要侵犯它信念的自由。

在这当中还常常有为了推行自己目的的特殊结合，其成员这时构成了一个道德人格，而会议的结论这时就不能再被看作一个自由多数的结论，而应看作一个派别的胜利：这个派别为了推行自己的事情，容许自己欺诈和一切种类的暴行，并把战败的一方当作叛乱者加以可怕的虐待；这样一类圣父的会议被它的对手叫作强盗团伙，而 Mosheim，[Institutiones] Hist[oriae] eccl[esiasticae] saec.
5, pars 2, c. 5, § 14，对这个严厉的说法只挑出一点来反对：它没有被同样用到另一些教会会议上，而那些会议同样配得上这个称号。
但自从俗人也失去了权利，在信仰方面连被代表一下都不行，自从基督教会的主教和首领成了纯粹的官员，自从那时起，信仰的法律就完全由他们的统治者制定，而人民——虽然不是主教们——可以对这一点相当无所谓：它在信仰上的统治者和审判者，是一个人——教皇——，还是许多不依赖它的人；它的属灵宪制，是君主制还是贵族制：它的权利在两种情况下都一样大，都等于零。
要为这样一种统治、这样一种在信仰事务上的宪制的合法性费一句话，完全是白费。

en: It is the first principle of the Protestant church that its contract rests on a general agreement of all its members, that from no human being can entry into a church contract be demanded whose condition would be that he subject his faith to the majority of votes.

Luther at the beginning of his great work did indeed appeal to a free general church assembly, but only then was the great principle of Protestant freedom, the palladium of its church, found, when the joining, the appearing at a council was rejected, not because one could be assured beforehand of losing one's cause there, but because it contradicts the nature of religious opinions that a decision about them could be made by majority of votes; that everyone has the right to become one with himself about what his faith is. - The faith of every Protestant must therefore be his faith because it is his faith, not because it is the faith of the church; he is a member of the Protestant church because he has voluntarily joined it and voluntarily persists in it; all the rights of the church over him rest solely on the fact that his faith is also its faith.
zh: 新教教会的第一条原则是，它的契约建立在它全体成员普遍一致的基础上，不能要求任何人加入一个教会契约，而这个契约的条件竟会是他必须把自己的信仰交给多数票去支配。

路德在他那部大著的开头虽然诉诸一个自由而普遍的教会会议，但新教自由的那条伟大原则、他们教会的镇教之宝，是到人们拒绝加入、拒绝到场参加宗教会议的时候才真正被找到的，这不是因为事先就能确定自己的事业在那里要输掉，而是因为宗教见解的本性不容许由多数票来裁决它们；每个人都有权自行想清楚自己的信仰是什么。 —— 所以，每个新教徒的信仰都必须是他的信仰，因为它是他的信仰，而不是因为它是教会的信仰；他是新教教会的成员，因为他是自愿加入它、自愿留在它里面的；教会对他的一切权利，都只建立在他的信仰也是教会的信仰这一点上。

en: If the Protestant church, when it drew up its law book, its constitution with regard to faith, has in all its actions remained faithful to this principle of its pure church right with unchangeable firmness, then it cannot be exposed to any reproach of unlawfulness.

But the teachers who founded it, and the officials that it gave itself and of whom there will be talk later on, were sometimes tempted to regard themselves not merely as such representatives of their congregations, and to act as such to whom their congregation had entrusted only the declaration of its will, but to regard their authority as more extensive, so that it was left to the congregations, according to their insight, to settle among themselves what the faith of the church was, - which is evident both from the fact that very many determinations in the symbolic books of the Protestant church are of such a kind that, because of the subtleties occurring in them, it is impossible that they could be regarded as an opinion acknowledged by the assent of the whole people, and are only the work of hairsplitting theologians, and also [from this: it] is known from history, how some of these writings came to be and were accepted as a norm of faith, that the matter was mostly negotiated among the theologians alone; in which only such laymen took part as were needed as holders of power to procure and secure sufficient authority for these books. - Two circumstances can be adduced here as a justification for the theologians, [first] that they had to give the symbolic books a more learned form, to some of their doctrines a finer determination, for the satisfaction of their members even against the Catholic church fighting with such weapons, and that the less learned part of their church could hand over to them such a treatment of its doctrines of faith, without thereby withdrawing anything from its unchangeable rights.

Against this, however, it can still always be said that the theologians could have kept their more learned proofs, their more hairsplitting distinctions, for their writings quite without prejudice to the cause of their church, since after all it was mainly only a matter of the legitimation of their faith, in that the people cannot be legitimated, as to the fact that it believes something, by grounds that it does not know; the symbolic books would, in a simpler shape, which then of course would not have offered its point so polemically against everything, have had more the standing of a norm of faith that, according to the solemn principle of the Protestant church, was acknowledged by the insight of the people itself as its faith - all the more since the weapons that do very good service at one time become unusable afterwards.

Thus the learned form of the symbolic books, from which the people never proved anything, but only the learned did, has now also become unusable in this respect, since in it the theologians of our day no longer present their legitimation either.
The people never needed these weapons, and the learned too now disdain them.
zh: 如果新教教会在拟订自己的法典、自己关于信仰的宪章时，在它的一切行动中都带着不可动摇的坚定，忠于它纯粹教会权利的这一原则，那么它就不会遭到任何不合法的指责。

但创立它的那些教师，以及它给自己设置的、后面还会讲到的那些官员，有时受到诱惑，不把自己只看作教团的代表、不把自己只看作那样行事的人——他们的教团只是委托他们表达自己的意志——而是把自己的全权看得更大，以为可以听任教团凭自己的见识，彼此商定教会的信仰是什么；——这一点既可以从下面看出来：新教教会的信条书里有很多规定，由于其中出现的种种烦琐精微，根本不可能被看作凭全体民众的赞同而得到承认的意见，而只是好钻牛角尖的神学家们的作品；也可以从下面看出来：从历史上人们知道，这些文件中的某一些是怎样产生、怎样被接受为信仰规范的，事情大多是只在神学家中间商定的；参加其间的只有那些作为掌权者所必需的平信徒，要靠他们才能给这些书弄到并保住足够的权威。 —— 这里可以举出两种情况来为神学家们辩护：[第一，]他们必须给信条书一种更有学问的形式，给其中一些学说一种更精细的规定，好让他们的成员自己满意，也好用来对付用这种武器作战的天主教会；而且他们教会中较没学问的那部分人，能把对自己信仰学说的这样一种处理交给他们，同时并不因此从自己不可动摇的权利里让出什么。

但与此相对，人们总还是可以说，神学家们本来完全可以把他们那些更有学问的证明、那些更钻牛角尖的区分留给自己的著作，而毫不损害他们教会的事业，因为这里主要要的其实只是他们信仰的正当性证明，而民众并不能因为自己相信什么就靠一些它并不了解的理由得到证明；信条书如果有一种更简单的形态——那样当然就不会那么论战性地对一切都亮出矛头——本来会更有一种信仰规范的威望，按照新教教会那条庄严的原则，这种规范是凭民众自己的见识被承认为他们的信仰的——尤其是因为，在一个时候很有用处的武器，后来就不好使了。
这样，信条书的那种有学问的形式——民众从来没有从它里面证明什么，只有学者才这样做——现在在这方面也变得不中用了，因为今天的神学家们也不再拿它来出示自己的正当性证明。
民众从来不需要这些武器，学者们现在也瞧不上它们了。

en: The other circumstance that can be adduced to justify the theologians in determining, alone and without this, what the faith of the people is, is that they can say that in the later books, in which the faith of the Protestant church is contained, they acted only as interpreters of the norm of faith previously adopted by the people itself, and that this office of an interpreter could likewise have been transferred to them without prejudice to the faith rights of the people.
And indeed, if only one sense could be attached to the interpreted passages of the norm of faith, then nothing can be objected against this office of theirs.

But if a doctrine is perhaps capable of two or more interpretations, and one of them has been adopted by the theologians, or if by them consequences have been deduced from a proposition with the strictest correctness and set up as doctrines of the church, then in this they have acted on their own authority.

For in order to know which of the two possible interpretations is in accordance with the sense of the church, the church had to be asked about it beforehand, and likewise with regard to the consequences, since it is an often, to be sure especially in disputes, little observed but correct canon of criticism that, even if consequences flow from a system however correctly, it must not for that reason be assumed of someone who is attached to this system that he therefore also professes these consequences.
zh: 还可以举出另一种情况来为神学家们辩护——他们撇开民众，单独去规定什么是民众的信仰——他们可以说，在那些包含新教教会信仰的较晚的书里，他们只是作为民众自己先前采纳的信仰规范的解释者行事，而解释者这个职务同样可以在不损害民众信仰权利的情况下交给他们。
当然，如果信仰规范中被解释的那些段落只能有一种意思，那就没有什么可以拿来反对他们这个职务。
可是，如果一条学说也许可以有两种或更多种解释，而其中一种被神学家们采纳了，或者如果他们从一条命题以最严格的正确性推出结论、并把这些结论立为教会的学说，那么他们在这件事上就是自作主张。
因为要知道两种可能的解释里哪一种合乎教会的本意，就必须事先去问教会，就那些结论来说也是一样，因为这是一条正确却常常——尤其在争论中——很少被遵守的批判准则：从一个体系里无论多么正确地流出结论，也不能因此就断定一个信奉这个体系的人也承认这些结论。

en: With regard to faith itself no social contract really takes place; one can indeed bind oneself to respect the faith of others, as property rights, but it is really a civil obligation to honour the right of the other to have freedom with regard to his faith; one cannot possibly bind oneself, and still less one's descendants, to want to believe something; for every contract is in the end founded in the will, - one cannot merely want to believe something, and the faith of the church must in the strictest sense be a general faith of this church, i.e. of all individuals.
zh: 就信仰本身来说，其实谈不上什么社会契约；人固然可以约束自己像尊重财产权那样尊重别人的信仰，但这其实是一种市民义务，即尊重别人在信仰方面拥有自由的权利；人不可能约束自己去愿意相信某种东西，更不可能替自己的后代这样做；因为任何契约归根到底都建立在意志之上，——人不能光是愿意相信什么，而教会的信仰在最严格的意义上必须是这个教会、也就是所有单个个人的普遍信仰。

en: If a society of human beings, if one or several states, as a church, makes a contract with another society, which in this respect is another state, even if they are again connected in other respects, or with members of its state, then on its side it has at least acted unwisely - for it has bound the condition under which the other is to fulfil his part of the contract to faith and thus to something changeable, and has through the form of the contract put itself in danger either of renouncing the first, holiest right of every individual and every society, to change its conviction, if it is much concerned that the other fulfil his duty, - or, if it changes its faith, then the duty of the other disappears, which was bound only to this condition.

With its own state members, if these as a whole change the faith, the state and the church indeed soon come to terms, and the Protestant citizens and peasants still pay the same dues, interest, tithes and countless other trifles that they paid to the Catholic church; for the divine service of the present church they must contribute these, and to set up and maintain it money is also required, - and to make gifts to a church or to grant it rights [with the condition that it remains the same] would be just as if someone wanted to beautify a spot on a river with the condition that the very same waves should always remain at the spot they now wash. - Well, but still to pay wax candles for this altar, where none are burned and used any more, still to deliver these dues to this monastery, in which there is no prelate and no monks any more, and countless such rights and onera besides, were yet really intended only for the Catholic divine service and faith; if this falls away, then the rights grounded on it necessarily fall away too, and by the fact that the dues that one must pay to the new church are levied in the same extent and as grounded on the same rights as in the old church, at least a great inequality in the dues of the members of one church has been retained, which one cannot call fair.

If the obligation of the contributors, of the feudal tenants and serfs is still now to be grounded on the fact that they were indeed subject to this abbey, this monastery, this parish, were bound to these dues, and that, since the present church has taken over all the property and rights of the former, they too have entered into it, then that obligation was nevertheless not directed against the individuals or even against the buildings of this abbey etc., but against them as members, as officials of the Catholic church, i.e. against the church itself, and since the contributors are no longer in this one, since the Catholic church is no longer here, the rights arising from it and bound to it should have fallen away with it.
zh: 如果一个由人组成的团体、如果一个或多个国家作为教会，与另一个团体订立契约——后者就此而言是另一个国家，即使它们在别的方面又有联系——或者与本国的成员订立契约，那么它至少从自己这方面说做得很不聪明——因为它把对方履行契约中自己那一部分的条件系于信仰、因而系于某种可变的东西，并且由于契约的形式而让自己陷入危险：要么，如果它非常在乎对方履行义务，就得放弃每个人和每个团体最首要、最神圣的权利，即改变自己信念的权利；——要么，如果它改变了自己的信仰，那么对方的义务也就消失了，因为那义务只系于这个条件。

对本国的成员来说，如果他们全体改变了信仰，国家和教会倒很快就对付过去了，新教的市民和农民照旧缴纳同样的捐税、利息、什一税和无数别的小零碎，就和他们以前向天主教会缴纳的一样；他们必须拿这些来供养现在这个教会的礼拜，而操办和维持礼拜也是要花钱的；——至于向一个教会送礼或者给它让出权利[条件是它保持不变]，那正好比有人想把河边的一块地方弄漂亮，条件却是同样的水波永远留在它们现在冲刷的那个地方。 —— 好吧，可是还要为这座祭坛付蜡烛钱，那里已经没有蜡烛再点燃、再使用了；还要向这座修道院缴纳这些捐税，里面已经没有教长、没有修士了；还有无数诸如此类的权益和 onera（负担），本来都只是为天主教的礼拜和信仰而设的；如果这个没有了，那么以它为依据的权利也必然随之消失；而由于人们必须向新教会缴纳的捐税，是按照和旧教会同样的范围、并且被当作以同样的权利为依据来征收的，这就至少保留了教会成员捐税上的一种极大的不平等，这种不平等不能说公道。

如果说缴纳者、采邑臣和农奴的义务现在还应当建立在这一点上：他们本来就臣属于这座大修道院、这座修道院、这个堂区，负有缴纳这些捐税的义务；而且既然现在的教会承接了先前教会的一切财产和权利，他们也就进入了现在的教会——那么那种义务本来并不是针对这些大修道院的个人、更不是针对它的建筑的，而是针对他们作为天主教会成员、作为天主教会官员的身份，也就是说，是针对教会本身的；既然缴纳者已经不再属于这个教会，既然天主教会在这里已经不存在了，那么由它产生、系于它的那些权利也就应当随它一起消失。

en: And if, for example, Catholics had still remained behind in such a reformed country, could the same dues still be demanded of them with right, - could the state demand them with right?
To this one they pay other dues, as citizens of the state; these church dues were never its. - The new church?
They can with right maintain that they are obligated only to the old one - and that they may contribute nothing to the new one either, since they do not belong to it.

The similar case takes place in many Catholic, for example the Austrian, lands, which especially since Joseph's edicts of tolerance has occasioned many disputes and embarrassments. - Are the non-Catholics bound still to pay the same dues that they previously paid to the church, the same fees for baptism, confession money, maintenance of the various requisites for Catholic divine service, as they were hitherto obligated to do?
No, say the Protestants, for they do not belong to the Catholic church, and what they paid, they paid to the church.
Yes, say the Catholics, they are still owing this parish, this monastery the same as before; these may belong to whichever church they like.

Here the Protestants argue from the reverse of the principles that their church asserts against its members, and the Catholics from the same ones that the Protestant church has in its mouth within itself.
zh: 又比如，如果在这样一个改革宗的国家里还留着一些天主教徒，还能有理由向他们要求同样的捐税吗，——国家能有理由要求这些捐税吗？
他们作为国家市民向国家缴纳别的捐税；这些教会的捐税从来就不是国家的。 —— 新教会呢？
他们可以有理由说，自己只对旧教会负有义务，——也不必为新教会出任何钱，因为他们不属于它。
类似的情形出现在许多天主教地区，比如奥地利各邦，这种情形尤其从约瑟夫的宽容敕令以来引起了不少争执和窘境。 —— 非天主教徒是不是还有义务像以前那样，缴纳他们从前向教会缴纳的同样捐税，为洗礼、忏悔费、维持天主教礼拜的各种需要而缴纳同样的手续费？
不，新教徒说，因为他们并不属于天主教会，而他们付的钱是付给教会的。
要交，天主教徒说，他们欠这个堂区、这个修道院的还是和以前一样多；这个堂区、这座修道院爱属于哪个教会就属于哪个教会。
这里，新教徒是从他们教会对自家成员所主张的那些原则的反面来论证的，天主教徒则是从新教教会在自己内部所讲的那些原则来论证的。

en: The same inconveniences arise when a church makes contracts with other states, as a church that has a determinate faith; if as such it wants to make something a duty for the other contracting party, then it has likewise bound this duty to something that it has the right to change, since at the same time it nevertheless demands that the duty of the other should remain the same.

Thus the Protestants have bought the freedom of their faith and divine service, in accordance with the imperial constitution, with much blood - but in all peace treaties the contract is always drawn up in such a way that the Catholic princes have taken upon themselves the obligation, toward the Evangelical and Reformed church, to protect its divine service and its property.
What the essence of the Protestant churches consists in, this they have solemnly declared in their confessions and symbols.

Since now these contracts are made with churches in so far as they believe something determinate, Piderit42) (if I am not mistaken) argued several years ago, to the great annoyance of the Protestants, as follows: the faith of these is [no longer] the same, as is evident from the writings of the representatives of their church, the most famous divines, in comparison with their symbolic books; therefore they can no longer claim the rights that have been assured to them by the Catholics in the peace treaties, for one contracted with the church that stated its determinate faith; and if the Protestants still want to assert the same rights as valid, then they must retain the faith of the church, renounce their right to change it and, where they have changed it, take the change back. - Such an otherwise consistent reasoning would be impossible, the Protestants would not appear to be bound in the freedom, which cannot be lost through any contracts, to improve their faith, if the princes who made the peace treaties had made the contracts not as heads or members of a church, with the assistance of the theologians, who were always at their side and took pleasure in such importance, but as princes, i.e. as heads of their states, not for their churches but for their states. - To have free exercise of religion and to be faithful to one's faith is a right in which the human being must be protected not first as a member of a church but as a citizen of the state, and to secure this for his subjects is the duty of the prince as prince; and no more divine right could the princes have demanded from the contracting parties as a duty on their side, which they of course unfortunately obtained only as victors, - and instead of the expressions in the contracts now reading that the Reformed and Lutheran church too should have lawful free exercise of religion in the German empire, they would more correctly have been framed so that the Catholic princes bind themselves not to disturb and encroach upon the free exercise of religion of the Brandenburg, Saxon etc. states; if one had also said the Brandenburg, Saxon church, it would have come to the same thing, for this means a state in so far as it is attached to a faith, no matter which, and so one would have had the pleasure, after centuries of barbarism and years marked by streams of blood shed for this right of faith, of seeing a fundamental article of the social contract, a human right that cannot be given up by any entry into any kind of society whatsoever, purely, developed and solemnly acknowledged in the contracts of nations. - In the high feeling of the right of each individual and therefore also of all, i.e. of the church, to improve its faith, to advance further in its conviction, and on the other side at the same time with the feeling of how much one has given away of this right, that all those contracts of the church with foreign states were made for the church adhering to the symbolic books, and into what inconsistencies against that eternal right the church state falls when it believes within itself that the whole contract of this state rests on certain symbols and therefore holds it a duty to preserve with zeal the punctual faith in them, - great men in more recent times have vindicated for the concept of the name of Protestants the sense that it signifies a human being or a church that has not bound itself to certain unchangeable norms of faith, but protests against all authority in matters of faith, against all obligations that would contradict that holy right; and if the church wanted to be content with this negative determination, then it would have the merit of having reminded the state of a duty that it otherwise misjudged, to protect the subjects' freedom of their faith, and of having defended in its stead what it neglected.
zh: 如果一个教会作为一个有确定信仰的教会同别的国家订立契约，也会有同样的麻烦；如果它作为这样的教会想把某种东西定为另一方缔约者的义务，那么它同样把这义务系于某种它有权改变的东西，因为它同时又要求对方的义务保持不变。
新教徒就这样用大量的血买来了他们信仰和礼拜的、合乎帝国宪法的自由；——但在所有和约里，契约的写法总是这样：天主教诸侯对福音派和改革宗教会承担起保护其礼拜和财产的义务。
新教各教会的本质究竟在哪里，这一点它们已经在自己的信条和信纲里郑重声明过了。

既然这些契约是就教会信仰某种确定的东西而言与教会订立的，那么皮德里特42)（如果我没记错的话）几年前就很让新教徒恼火地这样论证过：这些人的信仰[不再]是同一个了，这从他们教会代表、最著名的神学家的著作与他们的信条书相比较就可以看出来；所以他们不能再要求天主教徒在和约里向他们保证过的那些权利，因为人们当初是与一个说出了自己确定信仰的教会订约的；而如果新教徒还想主张同样的权利有效，那他们就必须保留教会的信仰，放弃自己改变这一信仰的权利，并且把已经改过的地方再改回来。 —— 这样一种在别的方面前后一贯的推理本来是不可能有的，新教徒本来也不会显得受缚于他们那任何契约都夺不走的、改进自己信仰的自由，如果缔结和约的诸侯不是作为教会的首脑或成员、在神学家们的协助下——这些神学家总在他们手边，而且喜欢处在这样一种重要地位——而是作为诸侯、也就是作为自己国家的首脑，不是为自己的教会、而是为自己的国家来订立这些契约的话。 —— 能自由举行宗教活动、对自己的信仰保持忠诚，是一项人必须作为国家市民、而不只是作为教会成员受到保护的权利，而保障臣民的这一权利，是诸侯作为诸侯的义务；诸侯本来也不可能向缔约对方要求比这更神圣的权利作为他们一方的义务，当然他们可惜只是作为胜利者才得到它；——而现在契约里的措辞是，改革宗和路德宗教会也应当在德意志帝国内有合法的自由宗教活动，其实更正确的写法应当是：天主教诸侯承诺不去打扰和侵害勃兰登堡、萨克森等等国家的自由宗教活动；就算人们说的是勃兰登堡教会、萨克森教会，结果也一样，因为这指的是一个国家，就它信奉某种信仰而言，至于是哪一种则不确定；这样一来，人们本来就有幸在数百年野蛮之后、在那些以为此项信仰权利流出的成河鲜血为标志的岁月之后，看到社会契约的一项根本条款、一项无论加入何种团体都不能放弃的人权，纯粹地、展开地、郑重地在各民族的契约中得到承认。 —— 近代的伟人们怀着对每个人、因而也对所有人即教会改进自己信仰、在自己的信念中继续前进这一权利的高度情感，同时又怀着这样一种感受：人们从这项权利上已经让掉了多少；所有那些教会与外国订立的契约，都是为那些依附信条书的教会订的；而教会国家如果在自身内部相信这个国家的整个契约都建立在某些信纲之上，因而认为有义务热心地守住对这些信纲的一字不差的信仰，就会陷入同那项永恒权利相矛盾的种种不一致；——正是怀着这样的感受，近代的伟人们为新教徒这个名称的概念争得了这样的含义：它指的是一种人或一个教会，它没有把自己束缚在某些不可改变的信仰规范上，而是对信仰事务上的一切权威、对一切同那项神圣权利相抵触的义务提出抗议；如果教会愿意满足于这个否定的规定，那它就有这样一份功劳：提醒国家履行一项它本来认不清的义务，即保护臣民的信仰自由，并且代替国家去捍卫它所忽视的东西。

en: Through every contract that the church makes with every single member or with some single members, or that every single member makes with it, if this contract concerns rights that properly occur only in the civil state, it becomes unjust toward itself — or toward individual members of it.

One does not exactly feel this, but it must sooner or later reveal itself, and then in vain does a citizen who leaves the church and thereby loses civil rights demand these back from the state, for the state had neglected to determine its rights, and since it let the church do this in its place, the church regards its rights as its own and asserts them as such, for it made what was sufficient for its purpose — the general right, freedom of faith and of divine service — valid only for a single case, for its own case.
zh: 教会同每一个或某几个单个成员订的每一份契约，或者每一个单个成员同它订的每一份契约，只要这份契约涉及那些本来只存在于市民国家里的权利，教会就对自己不公正——或者对它的某些单个成员不公正。
人们并不直接感受到这一点，但它迟早必定显露出来，到那时，一个退出教会、并因此失去市民权利的市民向国家要回这些权利也是白费，因为国家此前疏于确定自己的权利，而既然它让教会代替自己去做这件事，教会就把国家的权利看成自己的权利，并当作自己的权利来主张，因为教会把那个对自己目的来说已经够用的东西——普遍的权利，即信仰和礼拜的自由——只对单个情形、只对它自己的情形来主张。

en: But if the formation of a church in general cannot be regarded as a contract with respect to faith, yet out of the general uniformity of faith a church, a union for a purpose, arises of itself, then this purpose can be the protection and preservation of this faith, the ordering of a divine service that is in accordance with it, and the production in the members of those qualities that are in accordance with the churchly ideal of perfection.
zh: 但如果教会的形成一般说来在信仰方面不能被看作一份契约，而是从信仰的普遍一致中自行产生出一个教会、一种为某个目的的结合，那么这个目的就可以是保护和保存这种信仰，安排一种与它相合的礼拜，并在成员身上造出那些合乎教会式完善理想的性质。

en: As for the protection and preservation of faith — and what is meant by this is protection of faith and at the same time of the free exercise of divine service and of the maintenance of other arrangements — this is properly a duty of the state, and that protection, that guarantee, is necessarily contained in the social contract; and it is possible only in an ill-organized state or, as already said, in a state that has not known this duty, that has not claimed this right of protection for itself, that its citizens or a part of them can come into the position of having to assert this right by force also for their part, or of not being allowed to enjoy it.

In this position the Protestants found themselves, and the princes who courageously spoke and bravely fought against another part of the state power for the right of the free exercise of religion of their subjects did this out of princely duty; but about the inconveniences, that they concluded the peace and the treaties not also as princes, but as members or as heads of a church, we have spoken above.
Since the church therefore cannot protect its faith against force, nothing remains but to protect and preserve it against itself.
zh: 至于信仰的保护和保存——这里指的是保护信仰，同时也保护礼拜的自由举行和其他安排的维持——这其实是国家的一项义务，那种保护、那种保证必然包含在社会契约里；只有在组织不良的国家里，或者像已经说过的，在一个不知道这项义务、不曾把这种保护权利归到自己名下的国家里，才可能出现这种情况：它的市民或其中一部分人会落到不得不也为自己这一方用暴力去主张这项权利，或者不被允许享有这项权利的地步。
新教徒就处在这种情况下；那些针对国家权力的另一部分，为自己的臣民争取自由信教的权利而勇敢发言、英勇作战的诸侯，是出于诸侯的义务才这样做的；至于他们不是作为诸侯，而是作为教会的成员或首脑去缔结和约和各项条约所带来的不便，我们在上面已经谈过。
既然教会因此不能保护自己的信仰免受暴力，那就只剩下把它保护起来、保存下来，使它免受它自己之害。

en: If the faith that is to be protected is to be regarded as the general faith, from which one or another deviated wholly or in individual parts, then such a one would for that very reason no longer be a member of the church, and he would have renounced its benefits, just as it would no longer have any rights over him; but if it were nevertheless to have the right over him that he would be obliged to let himself be instructed by it and to obey its prescriptions as to what he should do or omit, then this right could be grounded only in this, that in the contract with the church he had bound himself for future cases to trust the majority of votes or the representatives of the church in the determination of the true faith and to let himself be guided by it therein; but this would mean ascribing to the church a kind of infallibility, and to protest against an authority of that kind is the highest duty of a true Protestant. — The one who thinks differently would here find himself in the case of a transgression of the civil laws, by whose holders of power he is forced to respect them; but of that kind the church contract cannot possibly be — it [sc. the church] can hold its faith, so to speak its laws, valid only for him who accepts them voluntarily, voluntarily believes and lives in accordance with them.

There remains only the case that the right of the church were grounded in protecting against this individual himself the faith to which he once professed himself, the general faith of the church — not insofar as it was the faith of the church, but insofar as it was once the faith of this individual.

The one who thinks differently is not so much in the case of the spendthrift, whose remaining property the state [takes] into its administration and oversight — here the state does not so much protect the right of the spendthrift against himself, but the right of the presumptive heirs or of the community, which would otherwise have to support him — the one who thinks differently is, in relation to the church, rather in the case of the madman, whom the state, among other important considerations, is also for that reason obliged to take care of, because he can no longer himself assert his right to a sound understanding and can never be regarded as having given it up, and so the relatives or the state take it upon themselves to set him right again; so the church too wants to assert everyone's right to its faith — but the case is still different in this, that it still depends on each whether he wants to assert this right of his; he absolutely cannot be regarded, like the madman, as unable to renounce the use of this right to a certain faith, and as if it were the duty of the church to install him in the enjoyment of it without his consent, nolentem volentem; everyone must, as by the state the person of full age is treated, be left to his arbitrariness to assert a right or not.
From these principles there follow the limits of the church's duty to protect its faith within itself.
zh: 如果要受保护的信仰应被看作普遍信仰，而某个人在整体上或在个别部分上偏离了它，那么这样一个人恰恰因此就不再是教会的成员，他就已经放弃教会的好处，正如教会对他也不再有任何权利一样；但如果教会仍然对他有权利，可以要求他有义务听教会的教导，服从教会关于他该做什么、不该做什么的规定，那么这种权利只能建立在这一点上：他在同教会订约时，就已为将来可能出现的情形约束自己，在确定真正的信仰时信赖多数票或教会的代表，并在这方面听任教会引导；可这就等于把一种不会犯错的性质归给教会，而抗议这样一种权威，正是一个真正新教徒最高的义务。——思想不同的人在这里就处在违反市民法律的情形中，那法律的掌权者强迫他去尊重它们；但教会契约不可能具有这种性质——它〔即教会〕只能对自愿接受这些东西、自愿照它们去信、去生活的人，主张自己的信仰，可以说主张自己的法律。
只剩下一种情形：教会的权利建立在这一点上——把一个人曾经公开承认过的信仰，即教会的普遍信仰，不是就它是教会的信仰而言，而是就它曾经是这个个体的信仰而言，保护起来，使它免受这个个体本人之害。

思想不同的人不太像挥霍者的情形——挥霍者剩下的财产由国家收归管理和监督，国家在这里与其说保护挥霍者本人免受自己之害，不如说保护推定的继承人或者本来得养活他的那个共同体的权利——思想不同的人对待教会，倒更像疯子的情形：国家除了别的重大考虑，也正因为疯子再不能自己主张自己有健全理智的权利，又绝不能被认为已经放弃了它，所以有义务照料他，于是亲属或国家就接手把他重新调理好；教会也同样想主张每个人对自己信仰的权利——但情形毕竟在这一点上不同：每个人究竟愿不愿意主张自己这项权利，仍然取决于他自己；绝不能像对疯子那样认为他不能放弃使用这项权利去信某种信仰，也不能认为教会在他不同意的情况下、不管他愿不愿意（nolentem volentem）把他送进这种享受里是教会的义务；每一个人都必须像国家对待成年人那样被对待，谁主张一项权利、谁不主张，都随他的任意。
从这些原则里，就得出教会义务的界限：在自己的内部保护自己的信仰。

en: It is not a duty of the church that would spring from the right of another, into whose enjoyment he would absolutely have to be placed, but only a duty insofar as it prescribes this to itself, full of the importance of its doctrines for mankind, full of an overflowing zeal to make them happy thereby.

What it can do, then, is to make arrangements so that everyone on whom it wants to extend its benefits is put in a position to arrive at knowledge of it; and it must depend on the arbitrariness of each to use these means, for to apply coercive means or punishments would mean wanting to force the good upon people by violence, as the Spaniards in America or Charlemagne in Saxony did.

And apart from the fact that in some Protestant lands those who neglect public divine service and the Lord's Supper are summoned before a court and, if the neglect occurs several more times, are punished; apart from the fact that in some lands in which the church was reformed by the state, no one was indeed to be forced to abandon his faith, but it was ordered on pain of punishment to attend the sermons of the new doctrines and then to judge for oneself; apart from the fact that in some regions the Jews, with whom one has in general never been strict, must from time to time, at least through deputies, attend Protestant divine service — apart from this, the Protestant church has on the whole kept within the limits indicated, whereas it is on the other hand the most hateful side of the history of Catholic lands how, and from what principles, those of a different mind were treated there as rebels against the church, whose faith, determined by majority of votes or by absolute power, is to be law for everyone, as rebels against the Godhead, whose office of judge the church presumed to administer in its place, in that here the church contract was entirely equated with the contract of civil society and the church state was granted the same rights as the civil state.
zh: 这不是教会的一项从别人的权利中产生出来的义务——若是那样，别人就非得被送进这种享受里不可——而只是教会自己给自己规定的义务，它满心想着自己的学说对人类多么重要，满怀着要让人类因这些学说而得福的过剩热情。
所以它能做的，就是作出安排，使每一个它想施以好处的人都有可能获得对它的认识；至于用不用这些手段，必须取决于每个人的任意，因为动用强制手段或惩罚，就等于像西班牙人在美洲、查理大帝在萨克森那样，想用暴力把善硬塞给人。

且不说在一些新教国家里，不去参加公开礼拜和圣餐的人会被传唤到法庭，如果一再缺席还要受罚；且不说在一些由国家改革了教会的国家里，虽然不该强迫任何人放弃自己的信仰，却以处罚相威胁，命令人们去听新教义的布道，然后自己去判断；且不说在一些地方，犹太人——人们对他们本来从来不认真——时不时至少要通过代表去参加新教的礼拜；——这些都不去说，新教教会大体上还是守住了上面所说的界限，而天主教国家历史上最可恨的一面恰恰是：在那里，思想不同的人怎样、根据什么原则被当作反叛教会的人来对待——教会的信仰由多数票或绝对权力来确定，据说对每个人都是法律——又被当作反叛神性的人来对待，而教会竟僭取神性的审判权，代替神来行使；因为在这里，教会契约被完全等同于市民社会的契约，教会国家被授予和市民国家同等的权利。

en: With regard to these arrangements for preserving its doctrine, a contract can indeed take place, i.e. it can here be left to the majority of votes, to representatives or to the prince to organize these arrangements according to their insights, to examine and appoint the teachers of the people.

Whether this church can have the right to [depose] an official whom it has appointed, but who with his congregation has moved away from the church's doctrinal concept and renounces the church — about that there can be no question at all, for this congregation now forms a church for itself, over which another church can absolutely have no power, which can be regarded as a power-wielding state only within itself.

The new congregation owes this church, and perhaps also the state, at most the declaration that it has separated from that one, but a justification to neither of the two; and if the old church wanted not to recognize this separation, wanted to call the state to help in order to prevent it, which it has close at hand, because a ruling church is one that exercises the rights of the state to its own advantage, then it would be the indispensable duty of the state to protect the new church in the freedom of its faith and the exercise of its divine service.
Another question is — one that in recent times has gained a very widespread interest — whether the heads of the church, when they notice mischief, can take office and bread from such a preacher.

They assert quite consistently that it is their duty to protect the faith of the church and to see to it that this faith is taught; a preacher who teaches otherwise is therefore not fit for an office.

In the Catholic church this right of the church is absolutely not disputed; in the Protestant church, on the other hand, many argue against it on the ground that it would bring the church infinitely more honour if it made virtue and truth in general the purpose of its arrangements, and that it is against the nature of these two to want to bind them to determinate symbols; into the souls of those who have undertaken this and who still assert it, no ray of what is called truth has ever fallen; if a church and its heads and those of the state made virtue and truth the goal of their striving, then it would never happen that they tormented a righteous, active man, zealous for the good and the morality of his congregation, who however did not bind himself exactly to the church's doctrinal concept of his congregation; they would consider it a shame not to be able to get along with such a man; all they would do could be to recommend to him imitation of them in this, namely prudence, i.e. consideration for the opinions of others, and if he were worthy of such heads of the church and of the state, or they worthy of him, this advice would hardly even be needed.
zh: 至于这些保存自己学说的安排，确实可以有一份契约，也就是说，这里可以交给多数票、代表或君主，让他们按自己的见识去组织这些安排，审查并任命民众的教师。
至于这个教会是否有权〔免去〕它任命的一个官员——这个官员却和他的教团一起偏离了教会的教义概念，并声明脱离教会——那是根本不成问题的，因为这个教团现在自己形成了一个教会，另一个教会对它绝对不可能有任何权力，另一个教会只能在自己的内部被看作一个行使权力的国家。
新的教团对那个教会、也许还对国家，最多只欠一句声明，说自己已经同那个教会分离了，对两者都不欠任何辩解；如果旧教会不肯承认这种分离，想叫国家来帮忙阻止它——国家就在它手边，因为一个占统治地位的教会，指的就是一个为自己的好处行使国家权利的教会——那么国家就有不可推卸的义务，保护新教会在信仰上的自由和举行礼拜的自由。
另一个问题——它在晚近获得了非常广泛的关注——是：教会的首脑们一旦察觉到乱子，能不能撤掉这样一个传教士的职务和饭碗。
他们十分一贯地主张，保护教会信仰、并保证这种信仰得到传授，是他们的义务；所以一个教得不一样的传教士，就不适合当官员。

在天主教会里，教会的这项权利绝对没有人争辩；相反，在新教教会里，许多人反对它，理由是：如果教会把美德和真理本身当作自己安排的目的，那会给它带来无穷的荣誉，而且硬要把这两者绑在确定的信条上，是违背它们本性的；那些干过这件事、至今还这样主张的人，灵魂里从来没有落进过一丝配得上真理之名的光；如果一个教会以及它和国家的首脑们把美德和真理当作自己努力的目标，那就根本不会发生这样的事：去刁难一个正直、勤勉、热心于自己教团之善和道德的人，只因为他不肯严格拘守自己教团的教会教义；他们会觉得，跟这样一个人合不来是可耻的；他们所能做的，至多是劝他在这件事上仿效他们，也就是精明，即容让别人的意见；而如果他配得上这样的教会和国家首脑，或者他们配得上他，那这点劝告恐怕根本就用不着。

en: The most effective and therefore also frequently applied means of protecting the faith of the church is to remove the possibility that its members might hit upon doubts, upon other opinions of faith.

That such doubts, which would spring from the understanding's and reason's own activity, are prevented from within, i.e. in themselves, [for that] sufficient provision is made in manifold ways: by the fact that the youthful soul receives its first impressions, which throughout the whole life always retain a certain power over the human being, from the church; that the doctrines of the church are armed with all the terrors of the imagination; that they, as certain sorcerers are supposed to be able to check the use of the bodily powers, are able to paralyse all the powers of the soul or to force them only in the direction of their images; further, through the little free culture of these powers themselves, through the complete isolation of the knowledge of the church doctrines, which, isolated in terrible majesty, utterly disdain kinship, mingling with other doctrines, dependence on other laws — an isolation such that, like two roads to different quarters of the heavens, they never meet, where on the one road, that of domestic affairs, the sciences, the fine arts, a man appears with the most profound and most agile understanding, with the finest acumen, with tender feeling, whom one no longer recognizes, of all this no longer perceives anything, when one meets him on the church road.
zh: 保护教会信仰最有效、因此也最常用的手段，是排除这样一种可能：它的成员会生出怀疑、会碰到别的信仰意见。

至于从内部，也就是在人们自身之中，防止那些从知性和理性自己的活动中生出的怀疑，〔对此〕已经用各式各样的办法做了充分的防备：办法是让年轻的灵魂从教会那里得到最初的印象——这些印象在整个一生中始终对人保有一定的支配力；让教会的学说用想象力的一切恐怖把自己武装起来；让这些学说，就像某些巫师据说能阻碍人使用身体的力量那样，能够麻痹灵魂的一切力量，或者只能把它们往它们那些形象的方向上逼；此外还有这些力量本身很少得到自由培养，还有对教会学说的知识被完全隔离出来——这种知识以可怕的威严孤立着，完全鄙视同别的学说的亲缘、混杂，鄙视对别的法则的依赖——这种隔离就像通往不同天区的两条路，永远不会碰头：在一条路上，即在家庭事务、科学、美的艺术那条路上，出现的是一个人，他有着最深刻最灵活的知性、最精细的敏锐、温柔的感受，可是当你在教会那条路上遇见他，你就再也认不出他，这一切他再也觉察不到。

en: From outside, the possibility of a change of faith is cut off by strict censorship, by book bans, etc., by preventing foreign opinions from being circulated in conversations, from lecterns or pulpits — for the church has the duty to protect everyone's property in faith, and this property is injured when one's own doubts or the grounds of others could tear it from the believer.

Every church gives out its church faith as the non plus ultra of all truth and proceeds from this principle — a faith, then, that one could smear into the brain like money, and so it is really treated as well — and according to the assertion of every church there is nothing in the world so easy as to find the truth: one need only take one of its catechisms into one's memory; and with it, it does not hold,
zh: 从外部，信仰改变的可能被严格的审查、禁书等等切断，办法是不让外来的意见在谈话中、在讲台上或布道坛上流通——因为教会有义务保护每个人在信仰上的财产，而如果自己的怀疑、别人的理由能从信徒手里把这财产夺走，这财产就受了损害。
每个教会都把自己的教会信仰说成一切真理的极致（non plus ultra），并从这条原则出发——这样一种信仰，简直可以像钱一样抹进脑子里，而它在现实中也是照这样被对待的——而按照每个教会的说法，世上再没有比找到真理更容易的事了，只要把它的一本教义问答记进记忆就行；而在它那里，这并不成立，

en: Only to the earnestness that no effort pales does the deeply hidden spring of truth murmur44)
zh: 唯有那不为任何辛劳所黯淡的严肃，真理深藏的清泉才向它涌流44）

en: it holds a public market with it, the river of church truth rushes noisily through all the streets, everyone can fill his brain from its water.
zh: 它拿它公开叫卖，教会真理的河水喧闹地流过所有街巷，每个人都能用它的水灌满自己的脑子。

en: 45) The dispensers of it are the church's teachers, who in this respect are also its officials; they call themselves servants of the divine word — [of the word,] because their knowledge is not drawn from their innermost life, because they are words that came to them — servants, because they are not lords, not lawgivers, but obey a foreign will.
zh: 45) 分发它的人，是教会的教师，他们在这个意义上也是教会的官员；他们自称上帝之言的仆人——〔言的，〕因为他们的学问不是从自己最内在的生命里汲取出来的，因为那是些传到他们这里的言；——是仆人，因为他们不是主人，不是立法者，而是服从一个外来的意志。

en: The kind of divine service itself can just as little as faith be the object of a social contract; for if divine service is taken in the proper sense of the word — as certain actions that are to be duties immediately toward God, not to be derived from other duties toward oneself or other human beings — then the voluntary recognition of such a duty must alone contain the ground of the obligation to it; and the insight that something is such a duty can by no means be left to the majority of votes; but for the ordering of the exercise of this universally recognized duty a reciprocal contract can be concluded, to leave this to the majority, which would be the case in a democratic constitution of the church, or in a monarchical or aristocratic church to entrust it to a government.
zh: 礼拜的方式本身，和信仰一样，不能成为社会契约的对象；因为，如果把礼拜按这个词的本义来理解——即把它看作某些应当直接成为对上帝的义务的行为，而这些行为不能从对自己或对他人的其他义务中推导出来——那么，对这样一种义务的自愿承认，就必定单独包含承担这一义务的根据；而认识到某件事是这样的义务，绝不可能交给多数票去决定；但为了安排这种普遍承认的义务的履行，却可以订立一种相互的契约，把这件事交给多数，这在教会的民主宪法下就会是实情，或者在君主制的或贵族制的教会里，就是把它委托给一个政府。

en: These different functions are usually and very naturally united: the clergy are not only free teachers of the church's truth, but at the same time officials to whom the church's duty of protecting its faith is entrusted, further priests, that is, those who partly in the name of the people bring the prayers, sacrifices, etc., to the deity, whereby one imagines one can put oneself in favour with it, partly thereby give the people guidance and thereby place themselves at their head.

Besides, it is still chiefly their office to bring about, partly through the dogmatic doctrine of the church, partly through its morality and other supervision and admonitions, what one calls piety, fear of God, and which therefore must have a different tone and stroke in every church.
zh: 这些不同的职能通常并且很自然地结合在一起：教士不只是教会真理的自由教师，而且同时是官员，教会的义务——保护自己的信仰——就托付给他们；此外他们还是祭司，也就是说，他们一部分以民众的名义向神性献上祈祷、献祭等等，人以为借此就能得到神性的恩宠，一部分则借此给民众作指导，并由此把自己放到民众的前头。
此外，这尤其是他们的职责：一部分通过教会的教条学说，一部分通过它的道德以及其他监督和劝诫，产生出人们所说的虔诚、敬畏上帝，而这些东西在每个教会里必定有不同的调子和笔法。
